# SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sqloom)

**Reading coverage:** All 12 PDF pages: Sections 1–6, all tables and figures/captions, Algorithm 1, references and Appendices A–F including both proofs and all four prompts. ## Research question

Single-database execution can reward SQL with the wrong meaning, while erroneous or underspecified references weaken training supervision.

## Method

SQLoom contrasts parser-legal tokens, question-aligned SQL fragments and coordinated clause edits against nearby mistakes. It mutates databases to expose output differences while preserving schema constraints, then combines these signals with staged fine-tuning, error corrections, replay and same-database training examples.

## Evaluation

Qwen3-1.7B is evaluated on official Spider/BIRD splits and three Spider perturbations, with three seeds, transfer tests and same-data objective ablations. Counterexample search allows ten sub-databases with 200 mutations each. Authors manually review flagged Spider annotations; evaluation labels remain unchanged.

## What the results support

The reported objective outperforms plain supervised learning on the same augmented data. Spider-Refined training yields smaller additional gains. The 378 reviewed issues include valid alternatives rejected by the comparator and questions underspecifying output columns; this selected audit does not measure general error prevalence.

## Limits and qualifications

A legal separating database proves query disagreement, not which query matches natural-language intent. Positive labels still rely on references or model verification; finite search and grammar support limit coverage. No user, clarification or refusal experiment is reported. Training requires 38,000 GPT-4 calls, and official artifacts remain unverified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An adjacent example of using counterexample verification and annotation repair for supervision, with explicit limits on semantic certification.
